description:
Noticed four times in one session, each time as a false alarm during a gate.

`Map.reverse/2`, `Range.reverse/2` and friends are private list helpers whose
clauses the coverage checker cannot prove exhaustive:

    fnp reverse([], acc), do: acc
    fnp reverse([head | tail], acc), do: reverse(tail, [head | acc])

    warning[type/no-matching-clause]: `fn` clauses don't cover every input
      --> runtime:Map.fz:191:3

Two costs.

The warning is emitted into the diagnostics of every USER program that reaches
one, so a fixture inherits noise about library internals it did not write and
cannot fix.

And because diagnostics goldens embed SOURCE LINE NUMBERS, adding any function
to a runtime-library module reblesses every fixture that touches it. Four times
this session a gate reported "3 to 6 fixtures failed" and the whole delta was a
line number moving because code was added above the warning. Each needed a diff
to establish it was nothing -- and one time in the same session a similar-looking
"goldens moved" WAS a real 25-fixture breakage, so the noise is not free.

TWO WAYS OUT, not exclusive:

  * make the helpers provably exhaustive, or annotate the parameter so the
    checker can see a list is the only input. That removes the warning at its
    source, which is where it belongs -- a library function should not warn the
    caller about itself;
  * stop pinning absolute line numbers for diagnostics that arise in
    runtime-library source. The fixture cares that the warning happened, not
    which line of a library it came from.

The first is the real fix. Elixir's own `List` helpers do not warn their
callers, and neither should fz's.

comments.text: Superseded and delivered by fz-5xp.87 in ca10f62f9. Every private runtime helper now has an explicit domain, the fixture matrix enforces that invariant, the full 658-case matrix has no runtime-source no-matching-clause diagnostics, and the 15 diagnostics sidecars made empty by the fix were deleted.

title: Runtime-library coverage warnings leak into every fixture that touches them
